skill.name: web-games
skill.description: Guides browser game development with framework selection, WebGPU planning, performance optimization, asset strategy, PWA support, and audio handling.
skill.summary: Plan web games that work well across modern browsers and devices.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Browser games require careful choices for engines, rendering, assets, audio, and offline support. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan practical web game architectures.
actual_capabilities: Compares Phaser, PixiJS, Three.js, and Babylon.js for browser game projects.
Explains when to use WebGPU with a WebGL fallback.
Lists browser performance constraints and matching mitigation strategies.
Recommends asset formats for textures, audio, and 3D models.
Covers PWA requirements for installable and offline browser games.
Summarizes browser audio handling requirements and best practices.
limitations: It provides planning guidance, not a complete game engine.
It does not include runnable sample projects or asset pipelines.
Browser support notes may need verification for current production targets.
It does not replace profiling on real devices and networks.

use_cases.title: Select a Game Framework
use_cases.description: Choose a 2D, 3D, or hybrid browser game framework based on project needs.

use_cases.title: Plan a Prototype
use_cases.description: Define initial rendering, asset loading, audio, and offline requirements before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Browser Constraints
use_cases.description: Check an architecture against browser limits for performance, storage, network usage, and autoplay rules.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a browser game framework for a 2D game. Compare Phaser and PixiJS for gameplay, rendering, and delivery needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Performance Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a browser game performance plan for mobile and desktop. Include asset compression, lazy loading, object pooling, batching, and worker usage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan WebGPU Adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a WebGPU adoption strategy for a new 3D browser game. Include WebGL fallback, feature detection, testing scope, and rollout risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Game Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this browser game architecture for framework choice, PWA readiness, audio handling, asset loading, and browser performance risks.

output_examples.input: I am building a casual 2D game with menus, sprites, and touch controls.
output_examples.output: Recommended direction: Phaser for full game features. Use compressed textures, lazy load levels, and pause gameplay when the tab is hidden.

output_examples.input: I need a plan for a 3D browser game that supports modern browsers and older devices.
output_examples.output: Use WebGPU where available, keep a WebGL fallback, detect navigator.gpu, and test asset budgets on mobile networks.

output_examples.input: Review my browser game launch checklist.
output: Add a service worker and web app manifest for PWA support.
Create AudioContext only after user interaction.
Compress textures, audio, and models before release.

best_practices: Choose the framework based on game type, engine needs, and rendering depth.
Use feature detection and fallbacks for graphics APIs.
Profile assets, loading, audio, and frame pacing on target devices.
anti_patterns: Loading all assets before the first playable screen.
Ignoring tab visibility, autoplay rules, and mobile data limits.
Assuming WebGPU support without a fallback path.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a full game?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning and review for browser game development choices.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Phaser, PixiJS, Three.js, Babylon.js, and raw Canvas or WebGL options.

faq.question: Does it recommend WebGPU for every game?
faq.answer: No. It recommends WebGPU for new projects when a WebGL fallback is practical.

faq.question: Can it help with mobile performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights asset compression, lazy loading, object pooling, batching, and worker usage.

faq.question: Does it include PWA guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers service workers, web app manifests, HTTPS, offline play, and installability.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
